name: Google Shape;62;p5
text:
NFC-only authentication
Relied primarily on NFC UID verification.

name: Google Shape;63;p5
text: “The panel questioned the reliability of using only NFC because NFC UIDs may be cloned or misused.”

name: Google Shape;64;p5
text: Added PIN authentication as the second factor and QR credential-integrity validation for High-Security Mode.

name: Google Shape;67;p5
text:
Human-in-the-Loop
Security personnel manually confirmed student identity.

name: Google Shape;68;p5
text: “The panel suggested removing heavy reliance on human-in-the-loop validation.”

name: Google Shape;69;p5
text: Replaced routine manual approval with automated verification and alert-driven monitoring.

name: Google Shape;72;p5
text:
Risk-Based Verification Modes
Used one verification workflow regardless of traffic.

name: Google Shape;73;p5
text: “The panel raised concerns about high-traffic entry and practical deployment.”

name: Google Shape;74;p5
text: Implemented configurable Fast, Standard, and High-Security modes.

name: Google Shape;77;p5
text:
Entry/Exit Monitoring
Recorded entry and attendance without state tracking.

name: Google Shape;78;p5
text: “The panel suggested monitoring for both entrance and exit.”

name: Google Shape;79;p5
text: Added Entry/Exit state tracking and automated Anti-Tailgating enforcement.

name: Google Shape;82;p5
text:
Restricted Event Access
Attendance was recorded without validating rosters.

name: Google Shape;83;p5
text: “The panel asked what happens if an official memo limits an event to selected attendees only.”

name: Google Shape;84;p5
text: Added registration validation for restricted events.

name: Google Shape;97;p6
text: Using NFC, PIN Authentication, and QR Credential Validation

name: Google Shape;99;p6
text: Justine G. Mendoza • Michael Daniel M. Milallos • Seanne Stiffel T. Sintay

name: Google Shape;100;p6
text: BS Computer Science | Adviser: Prof. Ferdinand Rubio

name: Google Shape;114;p7
text:
The Problem
Manual ID checking at entry gates
No real-time database validation for inactive or expelled students
Borrowed, lost, or cloned credentials easily bypass visual inspection
Paper-based event attendance systems
Severe queue bottlenecks and proxy attendance
Inability to enforce pre-approved, restricted event rosters in real time
Vulnerabilities of single-factor identification
Physical card possession alone cannot guarantee the bearer's true identity
Manual transaction-by-transaction guard approvals create operational delays

name: Google Shape;118;p7
text:
The Solution
Multi-Factor Architecture: NFC (possession) + PIN (knowledge) + QR (credential integrity)
Configurable Risk-Based Modes: Fast, Standard, and High-Security modes tailored to real-time traffic and security needs
Automated Gate Verification: Real-time database matching for enrollment status and restricted event eligibility
Alert-Driven Monitoring: Shifts security personnel from manual approvers to incident responders
Anti-Tailgating & Offline Resilience: Stateful entry/exit tracking with local shadow caching during network outages
Event Attendance & Reporting: Automated attendance recording with event-based reports and monitoring data.

name: Google Shape;131;p8
text:
GENERAL OBJECTIVE
To design, develop, and evaluate a Risk-Based Two-Factor Student Verification and Event Attendance Management System Using NFC, PIN Authentication, and QR Credential Validation.

FEEDBACK MECHANISM
System-generated logs, verification results, and security alerts provide information for monitoring and future system evaluation and improvement.

name: Google Shape;197;p10
text:
Research Methodology
A Developmental & Descriptive-Evaluative Approach

name: Google Shape;202;p10
text:
SDLC: Used Iterative Waterfall Model
Hardware: Integrated ESP32, PN532 NFC module, keypad, and webcam.
Backend: Developed local MySQL storage with Firebase cloud synchronization.

name: Google Shape;208;p10
text:
Controlled Testing: Measured transaction speed, authentication accuracy, and offline resilience.
ISO/IEC 25010 Model: Assessed Functional Suitability, Performance Efficiency, Usability, Security, and 4 other traits.

name: Google Shape;214;p10
text:
Method: Purposive and Convenience Sampling.
Sample: 80 targeted respondents.
Distribution: 70 CICT Students (end-users), 
5 Security Personnel (security monitors), and 
5 Faculty/Event Organizers/Administrators (event management and administrative users).

name: Google Shape;232;p11
text:
Hardware: ESP32 SoC + PN532 NFC module + 4×4 Keypad + USB Webcam.
Connection: Direct USB Serial (COM port) tether for low-latency data acquisition and 5V power.

name: Google Shape;240;p11
text:
Core Logic: Automated 2FA Engine, Risk-Based Mode Controller, and Anti-Tailgating Tracker.
Platform: Developed using C# and Windows App SDK (WinUI 3).

name: Google Shape;248;p11
text:
Primary (Local): MySQL database ensuring sub-15ms local query processing and offline operation.
Secondary (Cloud): Firebase Firestore via HTTPS for real-time offsite backup and synchronization.

name: Google Shape;256;p11
text:
Kiosk Interface: Fullscreen visual Pass/Fail output with instant feedback for students.
Security Console: Real-time push alerts exclusively for flagged exceptions (mismatches, tailgating).

name: Google Shape;289;p12
text: QR is a credential-integrity check — not a third factor.  Flagged credentials (inactive, expelled, graduated) are denied immediately in any mode, never escalated for a second chance.

name: Google Shape;317;p13
text: Live working system demonstration to follow the presentation.

name: Google Shape;337;p14
text: *Note: Backend database queries average only 15.42ms. Transaction times are influenced substantially by physical user interaction.

name: Google Shape;361;p15
text: Comparison with Traditional Methods & Related Studies

name: Google Shape;371;p15
text:
• High processing time leads to severe bottlenecking
• Vulnerable to manual errors and proxy attendance

name: Google Shape;385;p15

name: Google Shape;389;p15
text: The proposed system demonstrated higher estimated throughput than the observed manual paper-based process while adding stronger verification controls. This aligns with processing efficiency findings by Ajayi et al. (2024) and Sali & Okumuş (2024).

name: Google Shape;474;p18
text:
Multi-Layer Verification
Successfully integrated NFC (possession), PIN (knowledge), and QR validation to identify tested credential mismatches and apply the configured access rules.

name: Google Shape;478;p18
text:
Strict Physical Control
Entry/Exit State Tracking detected and blocked 8 simulated anti-tailgating violations, while the authentication workflow achieved 96.15% accuracy across the evaluated applicable authentication attempts.

name: Google Shape;482;p18
text:
Verification Mode Throughput
Fast Mode achieved 24.00 students/min, 9.38× the observed manual throughput. High-Security Mode achieved 4.23 students/min, 1.66× manual throughput while adding verification steps.

name: Google Shape;486;p18
text:
Offline Resilience
The local “Shadow Cache” allowed core verification to continue during simulated network disruptions, with offline transactions successfully synchronized after reconnection.

name: Google Shape;490;p18
text:
Alert-Driven Access
Automated database validation and access decisions, allowing security personnel to focus on monitoring and responding to system-generated alerts.

name: Google Shape;494;p18
text:
ISO/IEC 25010
Overall respondent evaluation: 3.81 (Strongly Agree / Highly Satisfactory) across 80 respondents, including students, security personnel, and faculty/event organizers/administrators, under controlled testing conditions.

text: The study establishes a functional technical proof-of-concept that provides a basis for future testing and system scaling.
